note: Append-only history. Never remove or overwrite existing entries here — unlike feed.json (which is a rolling last-90-days window for the live ticker), this file is meant to grow forever and power the on-page archive section. Each weekly update should add new items to the front of this array.

items.text: Operation Shamrock founder Erin West argues pig butchering scams run as a supply chain, not isolated crimes; PYMNTS cites an Arizona man who lost $4.5 million to an investment scam, and finds victims who report to their bank recover funds twice as often (42%) as those who go through police or federal channels (20%)

a third of merchants don't know whether Visa's Acquirer Monitoring Program (VAMP) affects them, and 20% admit they don't track their own TC40 fraud data, even though April's final rollout phase set acquirer penalties of $4 to $8 per card-not-present transaction once a portfolio crosses a 0.7% fraud and dispute ratio

Kelantan, Malaysia police logged 94 triangulation fraud reports (75 buyers victimized, 19 sellers whose listings were hijacked) in the run-up to mid-September; scammers use a real seller's online listing for a motorcycle, car, or phone to collect payment while the actual seller is dragged into a transaction they never made

Kenyan DCI detectives arrested 14 suspects, including three armed police officers who were providing tactical cover, in a Nairobi warehouse raid that recovered 65 fake gold bars, 156 bundles of counterfeit US$100 notes, and chemicals and printing materials for manufacturing forged currency

a collector paid $18,500 for a PSA 10 One Piece card listed directly through PSA's own eBay Vault account; PSA's Brand Protection team later determined the slab, label, and card inside were all counterfeit, and that it had never graded or encapsulated the item despite the vault listing

a federal judge denied Ticketmaster and Live Nation's motion to dismiss the FTC's ticket resale lawsuit, letting claims proceed into discovery that the company let brokers use thousands of fake accounts to bypass purchase limits and turned a blind eye to scalpers as a matter of policy

EU prosecutors say a Hong Kong and UAE based ring assembled phones from used components and shipped them to the Netherlands relabeled as new, causing an estimated 300 million euros in consumer losses and over 30 million euros in lost VAT; the raid spanned 160 searches and seizures across 19 countries and netted 7 arrests, including the two alleged leaders

South Africa's Hawks seized an estimated R7 million in suspected counterfeit Nike, Adidas, and Lacoste goods from a Gqeberha shop called Sneaker Freakz, following test purchases by brand representatives; the two shop owners face Counterfeit Goods Act charges and are due in court October 29

a BBC investigation found 45 TikTok accounts using AI-generated videos of injured veterans to sell cheap imported goods as handmade; one Wiltshire veteran paid £154.99 for a wooden flag that arrived as a printed plywood plaque shipped from China, and TikTok removed all 45 accounts once BBC flagged them

a Cloud Security Alliance research note built from a staging server obtained by Gambit Security found one operator used three chained open-source LLM tools to autonomously breach 105 e-commerce retailers and steal 600,000+ payment card records between July and September, spending roughly $25 per target
a Spreedly-backed survey of eCommerce merchants finds 51% expect fraud-staffing budgets to hold flat or shrink even as 63% plan to increase spending on fraud-management technology instead

Hong Kong police arrested four people, one with triad ties, over Pokémon card deals arranged on Facebook where sellers falsely claimed a buyer's payment had failed or landed in the wrong account to extract a second payment, netting roughly HK$101,000 (~US$13,000) across six cases

a wave of Pokémon card store break-ins and robberies is sweeping Canada, including a Winnipeg shop burglarized twice in a month (20,500 cards taken in the second hit) and a Central Alberta collector's binder holding a rare Umbreon ex, as seven-figure card sales fuel demand for loot that's compact and hard to trace
the Better Business Bureau is warning Southern Alberta and East Kootenay residents after a victim lost $700,000 CAD buying gold bars that turned out to be fake

a coalition of major banks (including Bank of America, Capital One, NatWest, ING, and Commonwealth Bank of Australia) warns AI shopping agents are outpacing consumer fraud and data-privacy protections, as one UK retailer's AI-agent traffic jumped from 0.3% to 2.5% of searches in a year

tracked an active cloud-intrusion campaign, running since May, that opens with a fake IT-helpdesk call pressuring an employee to re-register a passkey, then pivots into Microsoft Graph, SharePoint, and OneDrive data collection

synthetic identity fraud, which blends real stolen data with fabricated details into ‘Frankenstein’ identities, is emerging as one of the biggest threats to financial institutions, distinct from deepfake-based impersonation

a BrandShield trust survey of 1,029 US shoppers found 34.7% named TikTok Shop as the marketplace where they hit a scam or counterfeit purchase, ahead of eBay at 28.4%, and most cases involved brand impersonation

a BBC investigation found thousands of sellers wrongly suspended or permanently banned by its automated fraud-detection tools, including a seller banned over a £2 pair of sandals the AI wrongly flagged as counterfeit

a federal grand jury indicted 12 people, including Coolkicks’ co-founder and six former Nike employees, in a $2 million cargo-theft conspiracy that stole shoes from Nike’s Memphis logistics hub for resale

ringleaders of a $16.2 million scheme that swapped counterfeit iPhones stamped with stolen serial numbers into Apple Stores across LA to fraudulently claim AppleCare+ warranty replacements were sentenced to federal prison

an 84-year-old Delray Beach shoe store owner was arrested a second time after an undercover buy turned up counterfeit Louis Vuitton, Chanel, Hermès, and Goyard goods, over a year after his first counterfeit-sales arrest
the Postal Service Inspector General estimates $3.1B in revenue was lost to counterfeit postage labels between March 2024 and February 2026, with fake labels openly advertised for sale online

Mercari Japan is barring listings of sealed Pokémon TCG 30th Celebration products from launch day (Sept 16) to block scalper resale. Single cards stay listable, and the ban lasts until a safe trading environment can be ensured
researcher Frank McKenna has cataloged 1,300+ spoofed vehicle-dealer websites tied to $12.4M in reported victim losses; 600 have been taken down, with 5-10 new clones still surfacing daily
a credential-stuffing attack compromised 138,828 customer accounts in late July, exposing names, addresses, and partial payment card details
organized fraud rings are recycling forged identity documents and deepfakes across institutions, and one linked cluster spanned 70 identities across 13 devices
just 49% of firms use their bank-data connections to generate fraud alerts, even though 69% already use those same connections to verify account and routing numbers
new October terms double sellers' authenticity-proof window to 48 hours and give the platform authority to destroy items confirmed counterfeit after a six-week holding period
added a scam-verification tool to Alexa for Shopping that checks whether an email, text, or call claiming to be from Amazon is actually genuine
disabled direct messaging in its revamped Community forum after scammers used it to send fake "eBay Security Team" account-verification phishing threats
LA County Sheriff's raid on an Arcadia, CA warehouse seized roughly 25,900 counterfeit Nike, Adidas, and Fear of God Essentials items worth an estimated $10 million
a Miami-Dade woman was arrested a second time for selling counterfeit Chanel, Louis Vuitton, Hermès, and Gucci goods over Instagram DMs paid via Zelle
Pokémon Center is mass-cancelling bot-placed orders ahead of the 30th Celebration set launch, though shoppers report legitimate purchases getting swept up too
BOPIS (buy-online-pickup-in-store) fraud increased 65% year-over-year, as fraud extends beyond checkout into fulfillment operations
account takeover remained 2025's costliest fraud type at $15B+ in losses, even as victim count rose 18% to 6 million U.S. consumers
global chargeback volume climbed 41% from 2023 to 2026, rising from 238 million to 337 million annual disputes
retailers lost $706B to returns and $89B to shrink in 2025, with $100B of returns flagged as preventable fraud and abuse
the most common refund and policy abuse claim is a false item-not-received report, cited by 52% of merchants
card-testing attacks surged 175% year-over-year and account takeover attempts jumped 78%, as e-commerce fraud pressure rose 33% in the first four months of 2026
83.4% of enterprise merchants report friendly fraud has increased over the past three years, per its 2026 Chargeback Field Report
AI-generated damage claims are now the fastest-growing form of return abuse, as fraudsters generate convincing photos of torn or broken items to win refunds
reports of account takeover rose more than 36% in 2024 versus 2023, per Federal Reserve-linked suspicious activity reporting data
StockX intercepted 100,000+ suspected fake products over the trailing 12 months, including 40,000+ sneakers worth an estimated $30 million
Singapore Police report 477 Pokemon card scam cases since October 2025 totaling $958,000 in losses, as scammers exploit demand for new set releases with listings that vanish after payment

UK government research finds 1 in 4 pre-loved shoppers unknowingly bought a counterfeit last year, and new IPO guidance names Hermès, Louis Vuitton, Gucci, Chanel, and Prada as the most-targeted resale brands
PSA reports intercepting $200M+ in counterfeit and altered cards: a 1952 Mickey Mantle submits at a 62% fake rate, and Pokémon counterfeits are up 125% year-over-year
two Alabama residents sentenced for running a counterfeit precious metals scheme that defrauded victims across Alabama, Georgia, and Florida out of $120,000+
Fear of God Essentials posts a 95.75% unidentified (likely fake) rate in Entrupy's 2026 State of the Fake report, meaning nearly every submitted item can't be verified as authentic
Apple and London's Met Police tighten stolen-iPhone controls, and phone theft in Westminster is down 45.8% as Stolen Device Protection blocks resale-ready factory resets
post-purchase refund abuse overtakes payment fraud as e-commerce's #1 threat
orders placed by AI shopping agents jumped 1,247% year-over-year across one merchant network
organized "refund-as-a-service" crews are socially engineering merchant support for a cut of the item price
most chargebacks start as customer service failures, not fraud: the dispute only gets filed once support already dropped the ball
SEON wins Best AI Fraud & Risk Management Solution at Tearsheet's inaugural AI Innovation Awards
small merchants report near-impossible win rates against "friendly fraud" disputes, even with full delivery evidence
acquirers are rethinking blanket reserve holds as their main tool against deferred-delivery risk
Riskified partners with Marqeta to sharpen issuer-side decisioning on approved orders
cut its Purchase Protection dispute window from 100 days to 30 and doubled its human review team
sellers flag waves of orders from freshly created accounts within hours of each other, a card-testing pattern reported repeatedly on r/EtsySeller ahead of future chargebacks
moving to 7-day refund cycles and mandatory prepaid return labels to curb a growing wave of return fraud
a refund-fraud-as-a-service ring advertised openly on Reddit and Discord was busted for bribing insiders to approve fake refunds on items like MacBook Pros
AI-generated "vintage" photos are letting sellers dropship fast-fashion as premium secondhand finds on Vinted, undetected until the item arrives
claims shill-bidding on its live auctions fell nearly 80% over six months, but won't define what the figure actually counts
counterfeits still slip through StockX and GOAT's paid authentication pipeline, the gap that put Nike's lawsuit against StockX on the map
eBay card sellers report a rising AI-driven refund scam: buyers submit AI-altered "damage" photos to pressure a refund
counterfeiters are cracking open genuine PSA slabs, swapping in a lower-grade card, and resealing the case, so a cert-number lookup is the only reliable tell
triangulation fraud (fake listings that harvest card data to buy from real merchants) costs marketplaces an estimated $30B+ a year
AI shopping agents are being used for automated card testing and rapid bulk purchasing across marketplace platforms, per Unit 42
